H_hierarchical.evidence: The controller is explicitly organized with MAIN coordinating AUTO_MODE and MAN_MODE, plus motor function blocks; the HMI also separates Manual Mode, Automatic Mode, and Mode Selection.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Guards include mutual-exclusion interlocking for AutoMode/ManualMode, slot-number range evaluation for floor selection, slot-based rotation direction selection, and restart only after fault-cleared and safety-restored conditions.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: Actions include MC_MoveAbsolute/MC_Power/MC_Reset/MC_SetPosition, speed-parameter modification, motor enable/disable, HMI status/fault indication, and cyclic safety checks plus motor command dispatch.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: Emergency stop overrides motion commands, deactivates all motor drives, halts operation, forces a safe state, and restart is allowed only after the fault is cleared and safety conditions are restored.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: AUTO_MODE/MAN_MODE are introduced in Software §5.1, their variables in §5.2, HMI behavior in §6.2, safety behavior in §7, and parking/retrieval guards in §8.4.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as interlocking logic, manual mode, emergency stop, fault detection, and safe state imply control rules beyond a flat event list.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: Mode names are listed as POUs, while actions such as individual movements, predefined automatic sequences, HMI feedback, and shutdown behavior are described later in narrative prose.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: The paper describes Boolean interlocking so only one mode is active, slot-number range checks for floor/rotation decisions, and restart only after both fault clearing and restored safety conditions.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: MAIN coordinates communication between program blocks, while the cyclic task performs parent-level safety checks and motor command dispatch beyond AUTO_MODE/MAN_MODE internals.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: Emergency stop immediately deactivates all motor drives, overrides motion commands, halts system operation, and forces the system into a safe state across modes.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: The hierarchy is clear, but the paper does not specify a non-trivial initial pseudo-state or deep composite initialization chain.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: Slot-range guards, AutoMode/ManualMode interlocks, and fault/safety restart conditions would benefit from structured guard checking, but the paper does not provide three or more explicit arithmetic-Boolean formulas.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: Emergency stop and motor-fault rules cut across automatic mode, manual mode, and multiple motor substates; PLC fault signals are also continuously monitored.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: The model includes HMI status, alarm, fault indication, and progress feedback actions, though most actuator actions remain concrete motor or door commands.

key_nl_quotes: Interlocking logic plays a vital role within the PLC to confirm that only one mode can be active at a time.
When the emergency stop button is pressed, it immediately deactivates all drives of the motors and halts system operation.
one_line_pitch: This is a strong stress-test because it combines auto/manual hierarchy, slot-dependent guarded motion, rich motor/HMI actions, and global emergency/fault recovery spread across multiple paper sections.
rationale: The sample is not merely I/O wiring: the paper gives an executable PLC/HMI control architecture with MAIN, AUTO_MODE, MAN_MODE, slot evaluation, motion commands, and safety handling. Its hardest baseline traps are cross-section attribution, implicit industrial terms, and global emergency/fault behavior that must be duplicated or lifted correctly in a state-machine model. The global stop/recovery and parent-level monitoring make it especially favorable for pyfcstm forced transitions and during-aspect style modeling.
